instruction: I am a wheat farmer in Bathinda, Punjab. My soil test shows pH 8.2 and zinc 0.62 ppm (low). What zinc application is recommended?
output: For alkaline Punjab soils (pH > 8) with low zinc, apply 25 kg of zinc sulphate (ZnSO4) per acre at sowing, broadcast and incorporated into the topsoil. Pre-soak wheat seeds in 0.5% ZnSO4 solution for 12 hours before sowing for early uptake. Without zinc, expect 15-25% yield reduction on alkaline Punjab soils. Source: PAU Package of Practices.

instruction: When should I plant wheat in Bathinda this year?
output: The recommended wheat sowing window for Bathinda is 25 October to 15 November. Earlier risks heat stress at germination; later than 20 November risks grain-fill colliding with March-April heat waves. The 1-10 November window typically balances both risks. Source: PAU Package of Practices, ICAR-IIWBR Karnal advisories.

instruction: My wheat is showing yellowing leaves at tillering. What should I do?
output: Yellowing at tillering is most commonly nitrogen deficiency (older lower leaves) or sulfur deficiency (younger upper leaves). Apply 12 kg N per acre as urea topdressing for nitrogen, OR 8 kg sulfur per acre via gypsum or ammonium sulfate if upper leaves yellow. Avoid nitrogen in fog or cloudy weather. Also check for waterlogging. Source: PAU diagnosis guide, ICAR-IIWBR yellowing advisory.

instruction: What wheat variety is best for terminal heat tolerance in Punjab?
output: For terminal heat tolerance: HD-3086, HD-3226, PBW-725, PBW-Zinc-1. HD-3086 and HD-3226 from ICAR-IIWBR show 8-12% yield retention under late sowing versus older varieties like PBW-343 which lose 20-25%. PBW-Zinc-1 also has biofortified zinc. Source: ICAR-IIWBR variety release notes 2018-2024.

instruction: How much irrigation does Punjab wheat need and when?
output: Punjab wheat needs 4-6 irrigations totaling 35-40 cm. Critical timings: Crown root initiation (CRI) at 21 DAS, tillering at 45 DAS, jointing at 65 DAS, booting at 85 DAS, milking at 105 DAS, dough at 120 DAS. The CRI irrigation is the single most yield-critical (missing it costs 15-20% yield). With declining groundwater, drip or alternate-row irrigation cuts use 30%. Source: PAU Package of Practices.

instruction: When can I transplant rice in Punjab this year?
output: Punjab law mandates rice transplanting after 10 June (Subsoil Water Preservation Act). Recommended: 15-25 June for Basmati, 20 June - 5 July for non-Basmati. Earlier transplanting accelerates groundwater depletion. Direct-seeded rice (DSR) sown 1-10 June is the groundwater-friendly alternative. Source: Punjab government, PAU Package of Practices.

instruction: Should I grow cotton in Bathinda given climate change?
output: Bathinda cotton is currently optimal (boll formation Aug-Sep averaging ~32°C). Projections show this rising to ~34°C by 2050, pushing cotton into marginal viability. Heat above 35°C during boll formation causes shedding; sustained marginal conditions are projected from around 2029. Options: heat-tolerant Bt hybrids (RCH-650 tolerates 36-38°C), shift planting to April for earlier boll formation, or diversify with guar/pulses. Source: ICAR-CRIDA climate atlas, FAO ECOCROP.

instruction: El Niño is forecast this season. How does it affect Punjab wheat?
output: El Niño typically reduces northwest India winter rainfall 15-25% and raises winter temperatures 0.5-1.0°C. For Punjab wheat: (1) reduce nitrogen 10% to avoid lodging from rapid growth, (2) advance sowing 3-5 days to push grain-fill before March heat, (3) ensure two extra irrigations (CRI and tillering become more critical), (4) prefer heat-tolerant varieties like HD-3086. Source: ICAR-CRIDA ENSO advisories, IMD seasonal outlook.

instruction: How do I improve organic carbon in Punjab alkaline soil?
output: Punjab soils typically show OC below 0.5% (optimum 0.75%+). Best: (1) incorporate paddy residue with rotavator instead of burning (adds 0.05% OC per cycle), (2) green manure (dhaincha/sunhemp) in summer, (3) 5 tonnes FYM/compost per acre annually, (4) include legumes (mung/guar) in rotation. Expect 0.1% OC gain per 2-3 years of consistent practice. Source: PAU Soil Health Management.

instruction: How much wheat does Punjab grow each year?
output: Punjab grew wheat on 35.16 lakh hectares during 2023-24, producing 181.76 lakh tonnes, with an average yield of 51.70 quintals per hectare (20.92 quintals per acre). Wheat is the state's major cereal crop. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What temperature is best for growing wheat in Punjab?
output: Wheat is a cool season crop. For higher productivity in Punjab, the maximum temperature should stay within 15-22°C during the vegetative stage and 21-28°C during grain development. Minimum temperature should remain within 4-11°C and 7-13°C for those stages respectively. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What happens to my wheat if temperatures rise during the vegetative stage?
output: Higher temperature during the vegetative stage of wheat results in poor tillering and early heading, both of which reduce yield potential. Optimal vegetative-stage maximum temperature is 15-22°C in Punjab conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why does heat during grain filling hurt wheat yield?
output: High temperature during the grai filling stage causes premature ripening and reduces grain weight. The recommended maximum temperature for grain development is 21-28°C; sustained heat above this range cuts yield through smaller grains. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Can I grow wheat on alkaline soil in Punjab?
output: Wheat can be grown on most soil types in Punjab, but not o highly deteriorated alkaline soils or water-logged soils. For these problem soils, you'll need to undertake amendment (gypsum for alkalinity, drainage improvement for waterlogging) before reliable wheat cultivation is possible. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What soil should I use for durum wheat?
output: Durum wheat should preferably be sown on medium to fine textured soils. Avoid sandy or coarse soils where moisture and nutrient retention are inadequate for the crop's quality requirements. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What crop rotations work with wheat in Punjab?
output: PAU recommends multiple wheat-based rotations: Rice-Wheat, Cotton-Wheat, Maize-Wheat, Groundnut-Wheat, Soybean-Wheat, and longer cycles like Rice-Wheat-Summer Moong/Mash and Maize/Rice-Potato-Wheat. For groundwater-stressed areas, Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) or Direct Seeded Basmati Rice (DSBR) followed by wheat are also recommended. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I follow rice-wheat or cotton-wheat rotation in Bathinda?
output: Both Rice-Wheat and Cotton-Wheat are PAU-recommended rotations and work in Punjab. Cotton-Wheat is more groundwater-friendly than Rice-Wheat and is well-suited to South-Western Punjab including Bathinda. If you must continue rice, consider Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) before wheat to cut water use significantly. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which is the latest wheat variety from PAU for timely sown irrigated conditions?
output: PBW 872, released in 2025, is PAU's latest variety recommended for timely sown irrigated conditions. It has an average plant height of 100 cm, matures in about 152 days, and yields 24.4 quintals per acre. It is moderately resistant to yellow and brown rust and possesses bold, lustrous grains. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I have a poplar plantation on my farm. Which wheat variety can I grow under it?
output: PBW 872 (2025) is specifically suitable for growing under poplar plantation. It matures in about 152 days, plant height 100 cm, and yields around 24.4 quintals per acre under timely sown irrigated conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's the difference between PBW 872 and PBW 826?
output: Both are recommended for timely sown irrigated conditions and have similar plant height (100 cm). PBW 872 (2025) matures in 152 days with a yield of 24.4 quintals per acre and is suitable under poplar plantation. PBW 826 (2022) matures slightly earlier at 148 days with a yield of 24.0 quintals per acre. Both are moderately resistant to yellow and brown rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I sow wheat with Happy Seeder over rice residue. Which variety should I use?
output: PBW 869 (2021) is specifically recommended for sowing with Happy Seeder or Super Seeder in in-situ rice residue managed fields. Use 45 kg seed per acre. The variety has plant height 101 cm, matures in 158 days, and yields 23.2 quintals per acre. It has longer coleoptile, which helps emergence through residue. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why does PBW 869 have a longer coleoptile?
output: The longer coleoptile of PBW 869 helps the seedling emerge through paddy straw residue when sown with Happy Seeder or Super Seeder. This is critical in conservation tillage where seeds are placed deeper or beneath residue cover. The variety yields 23.2 quintals per acre when sown with 45 kg seed per acre. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which wheat variety is recommended for Bathinda district?
output: PBW 803 (2021) is the variety specifically recommended for cultivation in South-Western Punjab including Bathinda, Faridkot, Fazilka, Ferozepur, Mansa, and Sri Muktsar Sahib. Plant height is 100 cm, matures in 151 days, and yields 22.7 quintals per acre. It is resistant to brown rust and moderately resistant to yellow rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I farm in the South-Western region of Punjab. What wheat variety is best?
output: For South-Western Punjab (Bathinda, Faridkot, Fazilka, Ferozepur, Mansa, Sri Muktsar Sahib), PBW 803 is the PAU-recommended variety. It matures in 151 days, yields 22.7 quintals per acre, plant height 100 cm. It is resistant to brown rust and moderately resistant to yellow rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's the yield of Sunehri PBW 766 wheat?
output: Sunehri (PBW 766), released in 2020, has an average grain yield of 23.1 quintals per acre. Plant height is 106 cm, matures in about 155 days. It is moderately resistant to yellow rust and resistant to brown rust, suitable for timely sown irrigated conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which wheat variety has the highest yield among current PAU recommendations?
output: Among recently released varieties for timely sown irrigated conditions, PBW 872 (2025) leads at 24.4 quintals per acre, closely followed by PBW 826 (2022) at 24.0 quintals per acre. PBW 824 (2021) yields 23.3 quintals per acre. Yield differences are modest; choose based on disease resistance, days to maturity, and your specific farm conditions (residue management, plantation cover, region). Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How long does PBW 824 take to mature?
output: PBW 824, released in 2021, matures in about 156 days. Average plant height is 104 cm and average yield is 23.3 quintals per acre. It is resistant to brown rust and moderately resistant to yellow rust, recommended for timely sown irrigated conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Tell me about DBW 222 wheat variety.
output: DBW 222 is a 2020-released bread wheat variety recommended for cultivation throughout Punjab except sub-mountainous regions. Plant height is 103 cm, matures in about 152 days. It is moderately susceptible to yellow rust but resistant to brown rust. Average grain yield is 22.3 quintals per acre. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I farm in the sub-mountainous area of Punjab. Which variety should I avoid?
output: Avoid cultivating DBW 222 in sub-mountainous areas. While DBW 222 is recommended throughout Punjab generally, it is moderately susceptible to yellow rust which is more problematic in sub-mountainous regions due to the cooler humid microclimate. Choose other varieties like Unnat PBW 550 or HD 3226 which are resistant to yellow rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Compare DBW 187 and DBW 222 for me.
output: Both are 2020 releases. DBW 187 has plant height 104 cm, matures in 153 days, yields 22.6 quintals per acre, and is moderately resistant to yellow rust and resistant to brown rust. DBW 222 has plant height 103 cm, matures in 152 days, yields 22.3 quintals per acre, but is moderately susceptible to yellow rust (better disease profile favors DBW 187). Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want a wheat variety that is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. What do you recommend?
output: Several PAU varieties are resistant to both yellow and brown rust: HD 3226 (2020, 21.9 q/acre, 155 days), Unnat PBW 550 (2017, 23.0 q/acre, 145 days), PBW 725 (2015, 22.9 q/acre, 154 days), and PBW Biscuit 1 (2024, 21.1 q/acre, 157 days). Among these, Unnat PBW 550 has the shortest duration. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's special about HD 3226 wheat?
output: HD 3226 (2020) has good grain quality characteristics, plant height 106 cm, matures in about 155 days, and yields 21.9 quintals per acre. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust, making it a low-disease-risk choice for timely sown irrigated conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Is Unnat PBW 343 different from regular PBW 343?
output: Yes — Unnat PBW 343 (2017)  an improved version of the older PBW 343. Plant height is 100 cm, matures in 155 days, and yields 23.2 quintals per acre — better than the original. It is resistant to brown rust and moderately resistant to yellow rust. Recommended for timely sown irrigated conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want a short-duration wheat variety. Which has the shortest maturity?
output: Among PAU's recommended timely-sown irrigated varieties, Unnat PBW 550 (2017) has the shortest duration at about 145 days. Plant height 86 cm (relatively short, good lodging resistance), yields 23.0 quintals per acre. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. w during the 2nd to 4th week of November using 45 kg seed per acre. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When should I sow Unnat PBW 550 wheat?
output: Sow Unnat PBW 550 during the 2nd to 4th week of November (mid- to late-November). Use 45 kg seed per acre. The variety matures in about 145 days, plant height 86 cm, with bold grains and yields 23.0 quintals per acre. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's the plant height of Unnat PBW 550 and why does it matter?
output: Unnat PBW 550 has a relatively short plant height of 86 cm, which is helpful because shorter plants are less prone to lodging (falling over) under heavy fertilization or wind. It also has bold grains, matures in 145 days, and yields 23.0 quintals per acre with full disease resistance. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I have poplar plantation on my farm. List all wheat varieties suitable for growing under it.
output: PAU recommends three varieties for cultivation under poplar plantation: PBW 872 (2025, yields 24.4 q/acre, 152 days), PBW 725 (2015, yields 22.9 q/acre, 154 days, resistant to both rusts), and PBW 677 (2015, yields 22.4 q/acre, 157 days, moderately resistant to both rusts). PBW 872 is the highest-yielding choice. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Tell me about PBW 725 wheat variety.
output: PBW 725 (2015) has plant height 105 cm, matures in about 154 days, and yields 22.9 quintals per acre. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. The variety is suitable for growing under poplar plantation, making it useful for agroforestry farmers. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What about PBW 677? Should I grow it?
output: PBW 677 (2015) has plant height 107 cm, matures in 157 days, yields 22.4 quintals per acre, and is moderately resistant to yellow and brown rust. It is suitable for growing under poplar plantation. If you have poplar agroforestry, PBW 872 (newer, higher yielding at 24.4 q/acre) is generally a better choice now, but PBW 677 remains viable. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I still grow HD 3086 wheat?
output: HD 3086 (2015) yields 23.0 quintals per acre at 96 cm plant height and matures in 148 days. However, it is susceptible to new races of yellow rust and moderately susceptible to brown rust — disease pressure is a real risk. Newer varieties like PBW 872 (2025) or HD 3226 (2020) provide better disease protection at similar or higher yields. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want a wheat variety good for making biscuits. Is there o?
output: Yes — PBW Biscuit 1 (2024) is a premium special quality wheat variety bred specifically for cookies and biscuits. It has a spread factor of 9.8/10, medium soft grain texture, plant height 100 cm, matures in 157 days, and yields 21.1 quintals per acre. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What does spread factor 9.8/10 mean for biscuit wheat?
output: Spread factor measures how much a biscuit dough spreads when baked, with higher values being preferred for cookies and biscuits. PBW Biscuit 1's spread factor of 9.8/10 indicates excellent biscuit-making quality, combined with medium soft grain texture. The variety yields 21.1 quintals per acre and is resistant to yellow and brown rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I rely on just one wheat variety year after year?
output: No — PAU recommends growing multiple recommended varieties rather than depending on a single variety. Reasons: (1) disease resistance erodes over time as pathogens evolve, (2) different varieties suit different sowing dates, (3) genetic diversity reduces total-failure risk. Choose varieties matched to your sowing time and farm conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How do I pick the right wheat variety?
output: Three rules from PAU: (1) Grow recommended varieties — don't depend on just one. (2) Select varieties according to sowing time — varieties for timely sowing differ from those for late sowing. (3) Match special conditions: PBW 872, PBW 725, and PBW 677 for cultivation under poplar plantation; PBW 869 for paddy-residue (Happer) fields; PBW 803 for South-Western Punjab including Bathinda. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: If I sow late in November, which variety should I prefer?
output: For late November sowing (around 2nd to 4th week of November), Unnat PBW 550 is specifically recommended at 45 kg seed per acre. It matures in 145 days, yields 23.0 quintals per acre, and has resistance to both yellow and brown rust. PAU emphasizes selecting varieties according to sowing time, so don't use timely-sown varieties for late sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Is there a wheat variety that's good for human zinc nutrition?
output: Yes — PBW Zinc 2 (2023) is biofortified with higher grain zinc concentration, beneficial for human health. Plant height 100 cm, matures in 154 days, yields 23.0 quintals per acre. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust and has medium-dense ears with red glumes. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is the difference between PBW Zinc 2 and PBW 1 Zn?
output: Both varieties have higher grain zinc concentration for human health benefit. PBW Zinc 2 (2023) is the newer release: plant height 100 cm, 154 days to maturity, yields 23.0 q/acre, resistant to yellow and brown rust. PBW 1 Zn (2017) is older: plant height 103 cm, 151 days, yields 22.5 q/acre, resistant to brown rust but only moderately resistant to yellow rust. PBW Zinc 2 has the bettedisease profile. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Is there a wheat variety suitable for diabetic-friendly food?
output: Yes — PBW RS1 (2023) is a premium variety with high resistant starch in the grain. Resistant starch does not cause blood sugar spikes; instead it acts as dietary fibre, giving the wheat a low glycemic index suitable for diabetic-friendly products. Plant height 87 cm, mates in 146 days, yields 17.1 quintals per acre. Sow during 2nd to 4th week of November. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When should I sow PBW RS1 and what yield can I expect?
output: Sow PBW RS1 during the 2nd to 4th week of November. Expected yield is 17.1 quintals per acre — lower than standard varieties because the high-resistant-starch trait trades off some yield. Plant height 87 cm, matures in 146 days, resistant to yellow rust and moderately resistant to brown rust. Thpremium price for diabetic-friendly grain can offset the lower yield. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want to grow wheat that makes good chapati. Which variety?
output: PBW 1 Chapati (2020) is a premium bread wheat specifically bred for chapati. Chapatis are whitish, sweet, and stay soft for hours after cooking. Plant height 103 cm, matures in 154 days, yields 17.2 quintals per acre. It is moderately resistant to yellow rust and resistant to brown rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How should I fertilize PBW 1 Chapati if I have medium-textured soil?
output: On medium-textured soils, reduce nitrogen fertilizer by 25% from the standard recommendation and skip one irrigation when growing PBW 1 Chapati. This prevents lodging and protects grain quality. Standard practices would push the variety into excessive vegetative growth on these soils, hurting both yield and chapati quality. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why is PBW 1 Chapati's yield lower than other varieties?
output: PBW 1 Chapati yields 17.2 quintals per acre, lower than standard varieties (22-24 q/acre), because the variety is bred for chapati-making quality (whitish color, sweet taste, soft texture for hours) rather than maximum yield. Farmers growing for premium quality markets can recover the yield gap through better prices. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Are there durum wheat varieties recommended for Punjab?
output: Yes — two durum (Wadanak) varieties suitable for pasta making: WHD 943 (2011), plant height 93 cm, 154 days, yields 19.8 q/acre, and W 291 (2005), plant height 83 cm, 155 days, yields 19.4 q/acre. Both have low yellow berry incidence and field resistance to Karnal bunt. Sow on medium to fine textured soils for best quality. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Tell me about WHD 943 durum wheat.
output: WHD 943 (2011) is a durum wheat (Wadanak) suitable for pasta making. Plant height 93 cm, matures in 154 days, yields 19.8 quintals per acre. It has low incidence of yellow berry, is resistant to yellow and brown rust, less susceptible to leaf blight, and has field resistance to Karnal bunt disease. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is yellow berry in durum wheat and which varieties resist it?
output: Yellow berry is a quality defect in durum wheat where part of the grain becomes opaque and yellow, reducing pasta-making quality. Both PAU-recommended durums — WHD 943 (2011) and PDW 291 (2005) — have low yellow berry incidence. Sow on medium to fine textured soils for best quality. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Compare WHD 943 and PDW 291 durum wheat varieties.
output: Both are durum (Wadanak) for pasta. WHD 943 (2011): plant height 93 cm, 154 days, 19.8 q/acre. PDW 291 (2005): plant height 83 cm, 155 days, 19.4 q/acre. PDW 291 has broader disease resistance — yellow rust, brown rust, loose smut, flag smut, less susceptible to powdery mildew, leaf , head scab — plus field resistance to Karnal bunt. Both have low yellow berry. WHD 943 yields slightly higher; PDW 291 has better disease coverage. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is Karnal bunt and which varieties resist it?
output: Karnal bunt is a fungal disease affecting wheat grain quality and marketability, especially in durum wheat. Both PAU-recommended durums — WHD 943 (2011) and PDW 291 (2005) — possess field resistance to Karnal bunt. PDW 291 also resists loose smut, flag smut, and is less susceptible to head scab. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I missed the timely sowing window. Are ther-sown varieties?
output: Yes — PAU has specific varieties for late sown irrigated conditions. PBW 771 (2020) has plant height 80 cm and short maturity of 133 days, yielding 19.0 quintals per acre, moderately resistant to yellow rust and resistant to brown rust. PAU emphasizes selecting varieties matched to sowing time — don't use timely-sown varieties for late sowing as yield drops sharply. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Tell me about PBW 771 wheat.
output: PBW 771 (2020) is recommended for late sown irrigated conditions in Punjab. Plant height 80 cm (short, lodging-resistant), matures in just 133 days (short duration helps escape March-April terminal heat), yields 19.0 quintals per acre. Moderately resistant to yellow rust, resistant to brown r Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why is short duration good for late-sown wheat?
output: When wheat is sown late, the grain-filling stage gets pushed into March-April when temperatures rise above 28°C. Heat during grain filling causes premature ripening and shrunken grains. Short-duration varieties like PBW 771 (133 days) escape much of this heat by completing the crop cycle earlier, retaining yield. This is why PAU recommends specifically selecting varieties according to sowing time. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What are the special-purpose wheat varieties recommended by PAU?
output: PAU recommends four special-purpose timely-sown varieties: (1) PBW Biscuit 1 (2024) for cookies/biscuits, spread factor 9.8/10. (2) PBW Zinc 2 (2023) bioortified with grain zinc. (3) PBW RS1 (2023) high in resistant starch, low glycemic index for diabetic-friendly products. (4) PBW 1 Chapati (2020) for soft, whitish, sweet chapati. Yields are lower than standard (17-23 q/acre) but command premium prices. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want to grow biofortified wheat for my family's nutrition. What's the latest variety?
output: PBW Zinc 2 (2023) is the latest zinc-biofortified variety from PAU. Higher grain zinc supports human nutrition (zinc deficiency is widespread in India). Plant height 100 cm, matures in 154 days, yields 23.0 quintals per acre — only modestly below the highest-yielding standard varieties. Resistant to yellow and brown rust. Source: PAU Packagof Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want to grow wheat for pasta. What's the highest-yielding option?
output: Among durum (Wadanak) wheats suitable for pasta, WHD 943 (2011) has the higher yield at 19.8 quintals per acre versus PDW 291 (2005) at 19.4 quintals per acre. Both are resistant to yellow and brown rust, have low yellow berry incidence, and field resistance to Karnal bunt. Sow on medium to fine textured soils for best pasta-quality grain. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I have to sow wheat in January. Which variety can I use?
output: PBW 757 (2020) is recommended for irrigated very late sown conditions including January sowing in Punjab. Plant height 82 cm, matures in just 114 days, yields 15.8 quintals per acre. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. Yield is lower than timely sowing because the short cycle is needed to escape March-April heat. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is the shortest-duration wheat variety from PAU?
output: PBW 757 (2020) at about 114 days is PAU's shortest-duration wheat, designed for very late January sowing under irrigated conditions. Plant height 82 cm, yield 15.8 quintals per acre, resistant to yellow and brown rust. The trade-off is reduced yield versus timely-sown varieties, but it lets you produce a crop when normal sowing windows are missed. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Tell me about PBW 752 wheat.
output: PBW 752 (2019) is recommended for late sown irrigated conditions. Plant height 89 cm, matures in about 130 days, yields 19.2 quintals per acre. Ears are medium dense with red glumes. It is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I harvested paddy with a combine. The straw is everywhere. What should I do for wheat sowing?
output: Two PAU-recommended options: (1) Chop the straw with a paddy straw chopper-cum-spreader into small pieces and incorporate into the soil through tillage — no adverse effect on wheat yield. (2) Better: sow wheat directly into the standing paddy stubbles using Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, PAU Smart Seeder, or PAU Sface Seeder. Combine harvester should be fitted with PAU Super SMS. Do NOT burn paddy straw. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why shouldn't I burn paddy straw before sowing wheat?
output: PAU explicitly recommends NOT burning paddy straw. Burning destroys soil organic carbon, kills beneficial microbes, releases harmful pollutants (a major cause of north India's autumn smog), and wastes a free soil amendment. Instead, retain the straw and sow wheat directly with Happy Seeder/Super Seeder/PAU Smart Seeder/Surface seeder. After 3+ years of straw retention, you save 20 kg urea per acre and soil health improves. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is Happy Seeder and how does it help?
output: Happy Seeder is a tractor-drawn machine that sows wheat directly through standing paddy stubbles without burning or removing the straw. The straw remains as mulch, conserving moisture, suppressing weeds, and adding organic matter to the soil. PAU recommends Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, PAU Smart Seeder, or Surface seeding-cum-mulching for wheat sowing in combine-harvested fields fitted with PAU Super SMS. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How long do I need to retain paddy straw before I see soil benefits?
output: Retain or incorporate paddy straw through Happy Seeder for more than 3 years to see measurable benefits in wheat productivity and soil health. From the 4th year onwards, you can save 20 kg urea per acre because the soil organic matter cycle has improved nitrogen mineralization. If soil organic carbon climbs into the high category, drill only 27 kg DAP per acre at sowing instead of higher rates. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much DAP does my wheat need if my soil organic carbon is high?
output: If continuous paddy straw retention/incorporation has raised your soil organic carbon into the high category, drill only 27 kg DAP per acre at sowing — less than the standard rate. This saves cost without compromising yield because the well-fed soil supplies more nitrogen and phosphorus through mineralization. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want to remove paddy straw before wheat sowing. What's the recommended way?
output: If you must remove straw: cut left-over straw with a stubble shaver, sun-dry for 2-3 days, then collect with a straw baler that compresses it into bales. After collection or in manually harvested paddy fields, check soil moisture — if adequate, undertake tillage directly; if dry, apply pre-sowing irrigation (rauni) first. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is rauni?
output: Rauni is the local Punjabi term for pre-sowing irrigation applied to a dry field before tillage. PAU recommends rauni in paddremoved fields when soil moisture is insufficient for direct tillage, giving the seedbed adequate moisture for germination. After rauni, follow with disc harrow, planking, and cultivator passes to prepare the seedbed. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How should I prepare the seedbed for wheat after paddy?
output: After paddy harvest with straw removed: if soil has enough moisture, start tillage directly; otherwise apply pre-sowing irrigation (rauni). Use disc harrow once, follow with planking. Then give another cultivation with a cultivator. On heavy soils, do one more cultivation before planking. A tractor-drawn cultivator with pulverizing roller-cum-puddler can also be used to prepare a dry seedbed in one pass. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I grew maize. Now I want to sow wheat. How?
output: Wheat can be sown directly with a Super Seeder under flat-, ridge-, or bed-planted maize residue conditions. The maize residue gets incorporated by the Super Seeder, which improves soil health and wheat productivity without separate tillage operations. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is a Super Seeder?
output: Super Seeder is a tractor-drawn machine that incorporates standing crop residue (paddy, cotton, or maize) and sows wheat in one pass. PAU recommends it for direct wheat sowing after paddy (with PAU Super SMS combine), after cotton (after final boll picking with in-situ cotton residue incorporation), and after maize (under flat/ridge/bed planted residue conditions). Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I just finished my last cotton picking. Can I sow wheat right after?
output: Yes — sow wheat with a Super Seeder right after the final boll picking. The Super Seeder will incorporate cotton plant residues in-situ along with sowing wheat. This avoids the residue-burning step, saves time, and contributes organic matter to the soil. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I burn cotton residue before wheat?
output: No — PAU recommends in-situ cotton residue incorporation rather than burning. After final boll picking, use a Super Seeder which incorporates the cotton residues into the soil while simultaneously sowing wheat. This reduces field preparation time, conserves sorganic matter, and avoids air pollution. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is PAU Super SMS?
output: PAU Super SMS is a Straw Management System attachment fitted to combine harvesters. When the combine has Super SMS, paddy straw is properly chopped and spread during harvest, making it easier to sow wheat directly with Happy Seeder/Super Seeder/PAU Smart Seeder in the standing stubbles. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's the difference between Happy Seeder and Super Seeder for wheat sowing?
output: Both PAU-recommended for sowing wheat after paddy. Happy Seeder works in standing paddy stubbles when residue is left intact (a true zero-tillage approach). Super Seeder incorporates residue into the soil while sowing — useful for paddy, cotton, or maize residues. PAU also recommends PAU Smart Seeder and PAU Surface Seeder as alternatives for paddy-residue fields. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Do PAU machines for residue management really help with wheat productivity?
output: Yes — paddy straw incorporation or retention through Happy Seeder for more than 3 years measurably increases wheat productivity and soil health. Quantified benefits include 20 kg urea saved per acre from year 4 onward, and reduced DAP (27 kg/acre instead of higher rates) once organic carbon reaches the high category. The investment in machinery pays back through input savings and yield gains. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When is the best time to sow wheat in Punjab?
output: The first fortnight of November (1-15 November) is the optimum sowing time for wheat in Punjab. However, long-duration varieties can be sown from the 4th week of October to escape high temperatures near maturity. A delay of one week beyond optimum reduces wheat yield by about 150 kg per acre, so sowing on time is critical. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much yield do I lose by sowing wheat one week late?
output: Delaying wheat sowing by just one week beyond the optimum time reduces yield by about 150 kg per acre. The optimum window is the first fortnight of November in Punjab. Long-duration varieties should ideally be sown from the 4th week of October. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I want to sow wheat in mid-October. Is that too early?
output: Yes, mid-October is too early for most varieties. The recommended window starts in the 4th week of October (around 22-28 October) for long-duration timely-sown varieties — earlier sowing increases heat stress at germination and tillering. The full optimum window for varieties like PBW 872, PBW 826, PBW 824, Sunehri, DBW 187, HD 3226, Unnat PBW 343, PBW 725, PBW 677, HD 30 is 4th week of October to 4th week of November. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which varieties can I sow from the last week of October?
output: From the 4th week of October to 4th week of November, you can sow timely-sown varieties: PBW 872, PBW 826, PBW 824, Sunehri (PBW 766), DBW 187, HD 3226, Unnat PBW 343, PBW 725, PBW 677, and HD 3086 across the entire state. Avoid DBW 222 in sub-mountainous districts. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When should I sow Unnat PBW 550 and PBW RS1?
output: Both Unnat PBW 550 and PBW RS1 should be sown from the 2nd to 4th week of November (mid- to late-November). Earlier sowing exposes them to inappropriate temperatures, while their shorter duration handles the slightly later window well. Use 45 kg seed per acre for Unnat PBW 550 in conventional sowing, 50 kg per acre with Happy Seeder. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's the sowing window for durum wheat varieties?
output: Durum (Wadanak) varieties WHD 943 and PDW 291 should be sown from the 4th week of October to 1st week of November. This earlier window allows the durum's longer cycle to complete grain filling before terminal heat. Both have field resistance to Karnal bunt and yield 19.4-19.8 quintals per acre. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I missed November and now it's December. Which wheat variety should I sow?
output: For sowing from the 4th week of November to 4th week of December (late November through December), use PBW 771 (133 days, yields 19.0 q/acre) or PBW 752 (130 days, yields 19.2 q/acre). Both are recommended for late sown irrigated conditions and have short duration to escape March-April heat. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: It's already January. Can I still sow wheat?
output: Yes — for the first fortnight of January (very late sowing), use PBW 757. It matures in just 114 days and yields about 15.8 quintals per acre. Yield is reduced compared to timely sowing because the short cycle is needed to harvest before April heat damage. PBW 757 is resistant to both yellow and brown rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What seed rate should I use for wheat?
oput: PAU recommends 40 kg per acre for most varieties under conventional sowing. Use 45 kg per acre for PBW 869 and Unnat PBW 550. With Happy Seeder, increase to 45 kg per acre for most varieties and 50 kg per acre for Unnat PBW 550 (the higher rate compensates for some seed loss in residue). Always clean and grade seed thoroughly before sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why is the Happy Seeder seed rate higher than conventional?
output: Happy Seeder sows wheat through standing paddy stubble. Some seeds may not establish ideal soil contact due to residue, so PAU recommends slightly higher seed rates: 45 kg per acre (vs 40 conventional) for most varieties and 50 kg per acre (vs 45) for Unnat PBW 550. The higher rate ensures adequate plant population despite the residue cover. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why should I clean and grade my wheat seed before sowing?
output: Cleaning and grading wheat seed before sowing removes weed seeds, broken grains, and shrivelled or diseased seeds. This ensures uniform germination, full plant population from the recommended seed rate (40-50 kg/acre), and reduced disease and weed pressure right from emergence. PAU emphasizes thorough cleaning and grading as a basic requirement. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: My field has termite problems. How do I treat wheat seed?
output: For termite-infested soils, treat each kg of wheat seed with one of: 1 g Cruiser 70 WS (thiamethoxam), or 2 mL Neonix 20 FS (imidacloprid + hexaconazole), or 4 mL Dursban/Ruban/Durmet 20 EC (chlorpyriphos). Dry the treated seed in shade before sowing. Neonix has a bonus — it also controls smuts of wheat alongside termite protection. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which seed treatment controls both termite and smut?
output: Neonix 20 FS (imidacloprid + hexaconazole) at 2 mL per kg seed controls termites AND smuts of wheat in a single treatment. This is more efficient than separate termite and fungicide treatments. Dry treated seed in shade beforsowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How do I treat wheat seed for loose smut?
output: Treat 40 kg of wheat seed for loose smut using one of: 13 mL Raxil Easy/Orius 6 FS (tebuconazole) dissolved in 400 mL water, OR 120 g Vitavax Power 75 WS (carboxin + tetramethyl thiuram disulphide), OR 80 g Vitavax 75 WP (carboxin), OR 40 g Tebuseed/Seedex/Exzole 2 DS (tebuconazole). Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How do I treat wheat seed for flag smut?
output: Treat 40 kg of wheat seed for flag smut using 13 mL Orius 6 FS (tebuconazole) dissolved in 400 mL water, or 120 g Vitavax Power 75 WS (carboxin + tetramethyl thiuram). The same treatments protect against loose smut, so one application covers both diseases. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why dry treated seed in the shade and not in the sun?
output: PAU instructs drying treated wheat seed in the shade because direct sunlight can degrade the active ingredients in seed-treatment chemicals like thiamethoxam, imidacloprid, chlorpyriphos, and tebuconazole. Shade drying preserves the protective coating so the seed delivers full termite and smut protection at sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I'm sowing wheat after pearl millet, mustard, or other non-paddy/non-cotton crops. How do I prepare the field?
output: After other crops: apply pre-sowing irrigation (rauni), then give two cultivations/ploughings followed by planking. A tractor-drawn cultivator with pulverizing roller-cum-puddler can also prepare the dry seedbed in fewer passes. Then proceed with normal wheat sowing during the appropriate window for your variety. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which sowing window do I use if I'm growing PBW 803 in Bathinda?
output: Sow PBW 803 between the 4th week of October and the 4th week of November in Bathinda and other South-Western districts of Punjab (Faridkot, Fazilka, Ferozepur, Mansa, Sri Muktsar Sahib). PBW 803 is the variety specifically recommended for this region — yield 22.7 q/acre, matures in 151 days, resistant to brown rust, moderately resistant to yellow rust. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How early can I treat my wheat seed before sowing?
output: Do not treat wheat seed earlier than one month before sowing — earlier treatment reduces germination. Time your seed treatment with thiamethoxam, imidacloprid, chlorpyriphos, or fungicides like tebuconazole/carboxin to within 30 days of planting. A seed treating drum is the most effective application tool. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Can I apply biofertilizer along with chemical seed treatment?
output: Apply consortium biofertilizer after a gap of at least 6 hours from any pesticide seed treatment to avoid microbe kill. Inoculate one acre's seed with 500 g consortium biofertilizer and 1 litre of water on a pucca (paved) floor, dry in shade, and sow immediately. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Where can I buy biofertilizer for my wheat in Punjab?
output: PAU consortium biofertilizers are available at the Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana Seed Shop at Gate No. 1, and through the Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and Farm Advisory Service Centres located in different districts of Punjab. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why use biofertilizer on wheat?
output: Biofertilizers (like the PAU consortium) increase wheat grain yield and maintain/improve soil health over time. They supplement chemical fertilizers by adding beneficial microbes that fix nitrogen, solubilize phosphorus, and improve nutrient availability. Apply 500 g per acre with 1 litre of water to seed, dry in shade, then sow immediately. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What depth should I sow wheat at?
output: Sow wheat at a depth of 4-6 cm using a seed-cum-fertilizer drill. Maintain row spacing of 15-20 cm. For late-sown wheat, use 15 cm row spacing for higher plant density and faster canopy closure. Calibrate the drill accurately before use to ensure correct seed and fertilizer rates. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What row spacing should I use for late-sown wheat?
output: For late-sown wheat, use 15 cm row spacing instead of the standard 15-20 cm. Tighter spacing increases plant density to compensate for the shorter growing season and helps the canopy close faster, reducing weed pressure and conserving moisture. Sow at 4-6 cm depth with a calibrated seed-cum-fertilizer drill. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is a Lucky Seed Drill?
output: Lucky Seed Drill is a PAU-recommended implement that lets you spray pre-emergence herbicide along with the wheat sowing operation in one pass. This saves time and ensures the herbicide is placed at sowing for effective early weed control. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How can I help late-sown wheat germinate faster?
output: For late-sown wheat, soak seed in water for 4-6 hours and spread in a thin layer. Sow after 24 hours, making necessary adjustments in the seed drill. Soaked seed germinates and emerges faster, helping the crop catch up to the limited remaining growing season. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is bi-directional sowing of wheat?
output: In bi-directional sowing, sow half the recommended seed and fertilizer in one direction, then sow the remaining half across (perpendicular to the first direction). Use 4 cm sowing depth and 20 cm row spacing. The last ploughing in preparatory tillage can be skipped to offset the extra cost of double-sowing. The cross pattern improves canopy uniformity and yields. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is raised bed sowing for wheat?
output: Raised bed sowing uses a bed planter to sow two rows of wheat on a 37.5 cm wide bed with a 30 cm wide furrow between beds; rows are 20 cm apart on the bed. Use 30 kg seed per acre. Apply the entire nitrogen dose at sowing before preparing beds. Beds suit medium to heavy textured and water-logged soils, and improve water and fertilizer use efficiency while reducing weeds. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much seed do I need per acre for raised bed sowing?
output: Use 30 kg seed per acre for raised bed sowing — significantly less than conventional (40-45 kg/acre) because the precise placement on beds gives better establishment. Two rows are sown 20 cm apart on each 37.5 cm wide bed with 30 cm furrows between beds. Apply the entire nitrogen dose at sowing before bed preparation. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: My field has heavy soil and tends to waterlog. Should I use raised beds for wheat?
output: Yes — bed plag is specifically beneficial under medium to heavy textured and water-logged soils. The raised beds (37.5 cm wide, 30 cm wide furrows between) keep the wheat root zone above standing water, while the furrows drain excess water. Use 30 kg seed per acre, apply entire nitrogen at sowing, and the system also improves water and fertilizer use efficiency. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What benefits does bed planting give for wheat?
output: Bed planting offers several PAU-documented benefits: efficient use of water and fertilizers (rooted zone is precisely targeted), reduced weed emergence (drier surface between beds), mechanical weed control via inter-cultivation with tractor, and easy second-dose urea application during inter-cultivation. It is particularly suited to medium to heavy textured and water-logged soils. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is zero tillage sowing for wheat?
output: Zero tillage means sowing wheat without any preparatory tillage — directly into untilled soil after the previous crop. PAU lists multiple benefits: saved diesel antime, less environmental pollution, water savings during first irrigation, lower weed infestation (especially Phalaris minor), no leaf yellowing after first irrigation, easier timely sowing, and improved input efficiency. In weed-infested fields, spray 500 mL Gramoxone 24 SL (paraquat) in 200 L water per acre before sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How do I control weeds before zero tillage wheat sowing?
output: If your field has weeds before zero-tillage wheat sowing, spray 500 mL Gramoxone 24 SL (paraquat) in 200 litres of water per acre before sowing. This kills existing weeds without disturbing the soil, allowing immediate zero-till sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why is Phalaris minor less of a problem with zero tillage?
output: Phalaris minor (a major wheat weed in Punjab) thrives in tilled, disturbed soil. Zero tillage avoids the soil disturbance that brings Phalaris seeds to the germination zone, so weed pressure is naturally lower. PAU lists 'lower weeds infestation particularly Phalaris minor' as a documented benefit of zero tillage wheat. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why does my wheat turn yellow after the first irrigation under conventional tillage?
output: Conventional tillage churns the soil, and the first irrigation can cause temporary nitrogen tie-up and root stress, leading to leaf yellowing. PAU notes zero tillage prevents this — 'no yellowing of leaves after first irrigation' is one of its listed benefits. If yellowing happens with conventional tillage, do not over-apply nitrogen; check drainage and avoid irrigation in foggy/cloudy weather. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Compare conventional and zero tillage wheat sowing.
output: Conventional sowing uses a seed-cum-fertilizer drill at 4-6 cm depth and 15-20 cm row spacing after preparatory tillage. Zero tillage skips preparatory tillage entirely. PAU documents zero tillage benefits: diesel and time savings, less pollutn, less first-irrigation water use, lower Phalaris minor infestation, no leaf yellowing after first irrigation, easier timely sowing, improved input efficiency. Use 500 mL Gramoxone in 200 L water per acre before sowing in weedy fields. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I do zero tillage wheat year after year forever?
output: No — after 3 years of continuous zero tillage wheat, plough the field once to tackle perennial weeds or rodents that may have built up. Zero tillage offers many benefits (diesel savings, water savings, lower Phalaris minor pressure), but periodic ploughing every 4th year breaks pest cycles and prevents long-term issues. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What machine should I use for zero tillage wheat sowing?
output: Use a tractor-drawn zero till drill or strip till drill for sowing wheat in unprepared fields under zero tillage. These drills cut a narrow slot for seed and fertilizer placement without disturbing the surrounding soil. See Appendix III on Agricultural Engineering in the PAU Package of Practices for details. Source: PAU Package of Practicesabi 2025-26.

instruction: How do I prepare for Happy Seeder wheat sowing after paddy?
output: Two preparation steps: (1) Give the last irrigation to paddy crop two weeks before harvesting to ensure good soil moisture at wheat sowing time. (2) Either spread loose straw uniformly across the field manually, or harvest paddy with a combine fitted with PAU Super SMS so the straw is automatically chopped and spread. Then sow at 1.5-2.0 inch depth with Happy Seeder. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When should I give the last irrigation to my paddy if I'm planning Happy Seeder wheat sowing?
output: Give paddy's last irrigation two weeks before harvesting. This ensures soil moisture is adequate at wheat sowing time without being too wet for Happy Seeder operation. Timing this correctly is critical for good germination of wheat sown directly in standing paddy stubble. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What sowing depth should I use with Happy Seeder?
output: Sow wheat at 1.5 to 2.0 inch depth with Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, or PAU Smart Seeder in combine-harvested paddy fields. This depth balances seed-soil contact and protection from surface drying through the residue mulch. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is PAU Happy Seeder and how is it different from ordinary Happy Seeder?
output: PAU Happy Seeder is the upgraded version with a press wheel assembly attached to the normal Happy Seeder. It can sow wheat in combine-harvested paddy fields after cutting and spreading standing stubbles with PAU Straw Cutter-cum-Spreader. The press wheel uniformly places and presses chopped paddy straw in inter-row areas as mulch, leading to better germination, emergence, and vigorous initial establishment. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What row spacing should I use with Happy Seeder?
output: Use 8 inch (about 20 cm) row spacing when sowing wheat with Happy Seeder. This wider spacing improves weed control and yields better than tighter rows because it allows the residue mulch between rows to suppress weeds while wheat establishes well. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Tell me about Super Seeder for wheat sowing.
output: Super Seeder is a tractor-drawn machine that drills wheat seeds directly into combine-harvested paddy fields (with PAU Super SMS) or into cotton stalks after final boll picking — no straw burning or removal needed. It can also incorporate wheat residue in-situ. Drill 55 kg DAP per acre at sowing and prefer PBW 869 variety for sowing with Super Seeder. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much DAP do I drill at sowing with Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, or PAU Smart Seeder?
output: Drill 55 kg of DAP per acre at sowing when using Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, or PAU Smart Seeder in paddy-residue maged fields. This is higher than standard DAP because the residue can immobilize some phosphorus initially. Prefer PBW 869 variety for these conditions. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which wheat variety should I prefer for Happy Seeder sowing?
output: Prefer PBW 869 (2021) for sowing with Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, or PAU Smart Seeder. PBW 869 has a longer coleoptile that helps emergence through paddy residue. Use 45 kg seed per acre (50 kg/acre for Unnat PBW 550). Drill 55 kg DAP per acre at sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much extra seed do I need for Happy Seeder wheat compared to conventional?
output: Use 5 kg higher seed per acre with Happy Seeder than the recommended conventional rate. So for varieties needing 40 kg/acre conventionally, use 45 kg/acre with Happy Seeder. For PBW 869 and Unnat PBW 550 (which use 45 kg/acre conventionally), use 50 kg/acre with Happy Seeder. The extra seed compensates for some loss in residue. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When should I apply urea on Happy Seeder sown wheat?
output: Apply the recommended dose of urea immediately BEFORE first and second irrigations in Happy Seeder sown wheat. This timing ensures the urea is washed into the root zone with irrigation water rather than being volatilized from the surface mulch, maximizing nitrogen uptake. Also follow proper rodent control measures in Happy Seeder fields. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why are rodents a bigger problem in Happy Seeder fields?
output: The standing paddy stubble and uniform straw mulch in Happy Seeder fields provide cover and nesting habitat for rodents. PAU specifically warns to follow proper rodent control measures in Happy Seeder sown wheat fields (see Chapter 12 on Management of Rodents and Birds in the PAU Package of Practices). Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Can the Super Seeder also be used for cotton residue?
output: Yes — Super Seeder can drill wheat seeds directly into cotton stalks left after final boll picking, with no burning or removal of residue needed. The same machine works for paddy residue (aftecombine with PAU Super SMS) and cotton residue. It can also do in-situ incorporation of wheat residue itself. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's the right depth for sowing wheat with PAU Smart Seeder?
output: Use 1.5 to 2.0 inch sowing depth with PAU Smart Seeder, same as Happy Seeder and Super Seeder. The combine harvester for paddy should be fitted with PAU Super SMS so the straw is properly managed for direct wheat sowing. Drill 55 kg DAP per acre at sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: My soil has high pH and my irrigation water has high RSC. My rice harvest is delayed every year. What can I do for wheat sowing?
output: Medium to heavy soils with high pH and irrigation water having high residual sodium carbonate (RSC) cause poor infiltration. This delays rice harvest and consequently delays wheat sowing, hurting wheat productivity. Under these conditions, PAU recommends sowing wheat directly in standing rice/basmati rice (relay sowing) before the rice is harvested. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is RSC and why does it matter for my Punjab field?
output: RSC stands for Residual Sodium Carbonate — a measure of irrigation water quality. High-RSC water reduces soil infiltration rate, makes soil tight, and slows field drying. In Punjab, fields irrigated with high-RSC water (especially medium to heavy soils with high pH) experience delayed rice harvest, which then delays wheat sowing. Sowing wheat directly in standing rice (relay sowing) is one workaround. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Can I sow wheat into a standing rice crop?
output: Yes — under specific conditions where rice harvest is delayed (heavy soils with high pH and high-RSC irrigation water), sowing wheat in standing rice or basmati rice (relay sowing) is recommended by PAU. This avoids losing critical wheat sowing time when normal land preparation would push wheat into the late or very-late sowing window. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much wheat seed should I broadcast in standing rice for relay sowing?
output: Broadcast 55-60 kg of wheat seed per acre in standing rice or basmati rice. Time it just before or immediately after the last irrigation, during 10-25 October. Ensure sufficient soil moisture before sowing. Use long-duration wheat varieties recommended for timely sowing under conventional system. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is the right time window for sowing wheat in standing rice?
output: Sow during 10-25 October in standing rice or basmati rice, timed just before or immediately after the last irrigation to the rice crop. Use 55-60 kg per acre wheat seed broadcast uniformly. Ensure sufficient field moisture before sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Which wheat varieties should I use when relay-sowing in standing rice?
output: Use long-duration wheat varieties recommended for timely sowing under the conventional system. These would be the same varieties recommended for the 4th week of October to 4th week of November window — PBW 872, PBW 826, PBW 824, Sunehri (PBW 766), DBW 187, HD 3226, Unnat PBW 343, PBW 725, PBW 677, HD 3086. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How do I fertilize wheat that I broadcast into standing rice?
output: Apply the full recommended dose of osphorus along with half the nitrogen at the time of the first irrigation. Apply the remaining half of nitrogen at the second irrigation. If rain occurs, apply the 2nd nitrogen split immediately after the rain. The 2nd split of nitrogen must be completed within 50-55 days after sowing of wheat. Rest of the management package follows conventionally sown wheat. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: By when must I finish the second nitrogen split on relay-sown wheat?
output: Complete the 2nd split of nitrogen application within 50-55 days after sowing of wheat in any case, even if rain or other delays occur. Late nitrogen application beyond this window misses the critical tillering and stem-elongation demand period and reduces yield. The first nitrogen split goes with the first irrigation along with full phosphorus. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I broadcast wheat in standing rice. The rice was harvested with a combine without PAU Super SMS. What now?
output: If the combine doesn't have PAU Super SMS, you must distribute the lumps of loose straw manually across the field. Uneven straw piles create patchy germination and weak crop establishment. Spread the straw uniformly so the broadcast wheat seeds receive consistent mulch protection and moisture conservation. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is surface seeding for wheat after paddy?
output: Surface seeding-cum-mulching is a low-cost technique for in-situ paddy residue management. After combine paddy harvest, broadcast wheat seed and basal fertilizer uniformly over the field. Pass a cutter-cum-spreader which cuts the whole paddy straw at 4-5 inches above soil surface, providing complete mulch. Follow with irrigation to trigger germination. Use 45 kg seed per acre (treated with recommended pesticides) and 55 kg DAP as basal. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much seed and DAP for surface seeding wheat?
output: For surface seeding-cum-mulching of wheat, use 45 kg wheat seed per acre (treated with recommended pesticides) and 55 kg DAP per acre as basal fertilizer. Broadcast both uniformly in the combine-harvested paddy field, then pass cutter-cum-spreader to cut paddy straw at 4-5 inches above soil surface, then irrigate. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is PAU Surface Seeder?
output: PAU Surface Seeder is a low-cost machine that sows wheat seed and applies basal fertilizer in a combine-harvested paddy field while simultaneously cutting the standing straw. It consists of a seed and fertilizer box attachment with fluted-roller metering, mounted on a cutter-cum-spreader. After surface seeder pass, irrigate to initiate germination. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I don't have any of the PAU residue-management machines. Can I still do surface seeding?
output: Yes — if PAU Surface Seeder, Happy Seeder, Super Seeder, or combine with seeding attachment are unavailable, you can manually broadcast wheat seed and basal fertilizer after combine harsting, then pass a cutter-cum-spreader, then irrigate. The technique still works at low cost — just labor-intensive for the broadcast step. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What are the prerequisites for surface seeding to work well?
output: Two prerequisites: (1) Smaller plot sizes — ensure the field is leveled and divided into smaller plots before rice sowing/transplanting. (2) No excessive soil moisture at rice harvest time. To meet the second condition, give cut-off irrigation 15 days before harvesting transplanted rice, or 10 days before harvesting direct-seeded rice. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When should I stop irrigating my paddy if I plan surface seeding for wheat?
output: Cut off irrign 15 days before harvesting transplanted rice, or 10 days before harvesting direct-seeded rice. This ensures the field is not excessively moist at rice harvest time, which is one of the prerequisites for successful surface seeding of wheat. Excess moisture interferes with seed-soil contact and uniform straw spreading. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why is field leveling and small plot size important for surface seeding?
output: Surface seeding broadcasts seed and fertilizer uniformly, then cuts straw as mulch. Without proper leveling, water pools in low spots after the post-sowing irrigation, drowning seed in some areas while drying out others. Smaller plot sizes (made before rice sowing/transplanting) keep irrigation and germination uniform across each plot. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Compare surface seeding and Happy Seeder for wheat sowing.
output: Both are conservation-tillage options after paddy. Happy Seeder drills seed mechanically through standing stubbles (8 inch row spacing, 1.5-2 inch depth, requires PAU Happy Seeder or Super Seeder machines, drill 55 kg DAP/acre). Surface seeding broadcasts seed and basal fertilizer manually or with PAU Surface Seeder, then cuts straw at 4-5 inches as mulch (45 kg seed + 55 kg DAP per acre). Surface seeding is lower cost; Happy Seeder gives precise placement. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is the right approach to fertilizing wheat in Punjab?
output: PAU recommends an integrated approach: combine organic manures (FYM, compost), biofertilizers, and chemical fertilizers for higher crop productivity AND maintenance of soil health. Relying on chemical fertilizers alone leads to soil organic carbon decline; relying on organic manures alone is insufficient for current yield levels. Apply good quality farmyard manure (FYM) before sowing as part of this integrated approach. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why does PAU recommend integrated nutrient management?
output: Integrated use of organic, bio, and chemical fertilizers gives higher crop productivity and maintains soil health. Chemical fertilizers alone deplete soil organic carbon over time. Organic manures alone don't supply enough nitrogen and phosphorus for modern wheat yield levels. Biofertilizers add free nitrogen fixation and phosphorus solubilization. Combining all three is optimal. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When should I apply farmyard manure to wheat?
output: Apply good quality farmyard manure (FYM) before sowing wheat, as part of an integrated nutrient program that combines FYM, biofertilizers, and chemical fertilizers. The pre-sowing application gives FYM time to integrate into the soil profile before the wheat root system needs it. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I broadcast or place fertilizer at sowing under surface seeding?
output: Under surface seeding, broadcast both wheat seed and basal fertilizer (55 kg DAP per acre) uniformly across the combine-harvested paddy field. The cutter-cum-spreader pass after broadcasting buries the seed and fertilizer slightly under the chopped straw mulch, and the post-sowing irrigation washes them into firm contact with the soil. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much fertilizer should I apply to wheat on medium fertile soil?
output: Without a soil test, PAU recommends applying 50 kg N, 25 kg P2O5, and 0 kg K2O per acre to wheat on medium fertile soils. Sources: 110 kg neem-coated urea, plus either 55 kg DAP or 155 kg single superphosphate or 125 kg nitrophosphate per acre. Apply potash only if soil tests low. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I applied farmyard manure to my potato. Now I'm sowing wheat. How much fertilizer does the wheat need?
output: If wheat follows potato that received 10 tonnes of farmyard manure per acre, apply NO phosphorus and only half the recommended nitrogen — that's 25 kg N per acre, equivalent to 55 kg urea per acre. The residual nutrients from the FYM-fed potato cover the rest. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How does FYM affect wheat fertilizer needs in general?
output: Reduce the chemical fertilizer in wheat by 2 kg N and 1 kg P per tonne of farmyard manure applied. So if you applied 5 tonnes FYM/acre, reduce the chemical N by 10 kg and P by 5 kg from the recommendation. The savings come from the slow-release nutrients in well-decomposed FYM. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I added poultry manure to my rice. How much fertilizer does the wheat need?
output: If 2.5 tonnes per acre of poultry manure (or 2.4 tonnes of dried gobar gas plant slurry) was applied to the preceding rice, reduce wheat's N dose by 25% and P dose by 50%. So apply 37 kg N per acre (80 kg urea in two splits at first and second irrigation) and drill 75 kg SSP per acre at sowing — OR 28 kg DAP at wing plus 35 kg urea each at first and second irrigation. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What if I applied press mud to my rice? How does that change my wheat fertilizer plan?
output: If press mud (6 tonnes per acre) was applied to the preceding rice crop, apply 75 kg urea per acre to wheat in two equal split doses (at first and second irrigation), and drill either 28 kg DAP or 75 kg SSP per acre at sowing. The press mud's residual nutrients reduce the chemical fertilizer requirement compared to standard rates. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I'm sowing wheat after a leguminous crop like moong or gram. How much urea do I need?
output: After leguminous crops (moong, gram, etc.), apply 80 kg urea per acre in two equal split doses for wheat. The legume residue and biological nitrogen fixation reduce the wheat's nitrogen requirement compared to wheat after cereals. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Can rice husk ash or bagasse ash help my wheat?
output: Yes — apply 4 tonnes per acre of rice husk ash or bagasse ash to wheat before the last ploughing. This lets you reduce the phphorus dose by half (12 kg P2O5 per acre = 28 kg DAP or 75 kg SSP). Beyond saving phosphorus, the ash improves wheat productivity and soil health. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What is prali char and how does it help my wheat?
output: Prali char is biochar made from paddy straw. Apply 2 tonnes per acre of prali char to wheat before the last ploughing — this saves 35 kg urea per acre while increasing yield and improving soil health. It's a proctive way to use paddy straw rather than burning it. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I do a soil test before fertilizing wheat?
output: Yes — PAU explitly recommends applying fertilizer on a soil test basis. Without a soil test, use the standard recommendation for medium fertile soils (50 kg N, 25 kg P2O5, 0 kg K2O per acre), but soil testing lets you avoid both under- and over-application, saving cost and improving yield. PAU has a dedicated chapter on Soil Testing in the Package of Practices. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Do I need to apply potash to my wheat in Punjab?
output: Generally no — PAU's recommendation lists 0 kg K2O for medium fertile soils. However, if soil tests low in potassium, apply 12 kg K2O (20 kg muriate of potash) per acre. In Gurdaur, Hoshiarpur, Rupnagar, and Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar districts, apply 24 kg K2O (40 kg muriate of potash) per acre at sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I farm in Hoshiarpur district. How much potash should I add to wheat?
output: In Hoshiarpur (and also Gurdaspur, Rupnagar, and Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar districts), apply 24 kg K2O per acre at sowing — that's 40 kg muriate of potash per acre. These districts are known to need higher potash than the rest of Punjab. Apply at sowing along with full P and the basal urea. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: What's the difference between muriate of potash and other potash sources for wheat?
output: Muriate of potash (MOP, 60% K2O) is the standard PAU-recommended potash source for wheat. For 12 kg K2O/acre apply 20 kg MOP; for 24 kg K2O/acre (Gurdaspur/Hoshiarpur/Rupnagar/Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar districts) apply 40 kg MOP at sowing. Other potash fertilizers can substitute on an equivalent K2O basis (see Appendix IV in PAU Package of Practices). Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I'm using nitrophosphate. Do I still need urea?
output: When using 125 kg of nitrophosphate per acre as the phosphorus source, decrease your urea quantity by 50 kg per acre because nitrophosphate already contains nitrogen. So instead of 110 kg urea (the standard) plus phosphorus, use 60 kg urea plus 125 kg nitrophosphate. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: When and how should I apply phosphorus to my wheat?
output: Drill the entire phosphorus dose at sowing — either 55 kg DAP per acre or 155 kg single superphosphate (SSP) per acre. Drill it with the seed using a seed-cum-fertilizer drill rather than broadcasting. If using DAP, no separaterea is needed at sowing. If using SSP, apply 20 kg urea per acre at sowing as a starter. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Should I use DAP or single superphosphate for my wheat?
output: Either works. With 55 kg DAP per acre at sowing, no urea is needed at sowing because DAP already contains 18% nitrogen. With 155 kg SSP per acre at sowing, also apply 20 kg urea per acre as a starter dose because SSP contains no nitrogen. Choose based on availability and price; the agronomic effect on wheat is similar when applied correctly. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Why is no urea needed at sowing if I'm using DAP?
output: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate) contains 18% nitrogen along with 46% P2O5. The 55 kg DAP per acre supplies about 10 kg N per acre as a starter — enough to meet the wheat sdling's early demand. The remaining 40 kg N (out of 50 kg total) is applied as urea later, in two splits at first and second irrigation. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I will use single superphosphate for my wheat phosphorus. How much urea at sowing?
output: If using single superphosphate (155 kg SSP per acre) as your phosphorus source, apply 20 kg urea per acre at sowing because SSP contains no nitrogen. The remaining urea is applied later in splits at first and second irrigation. SSP is a good choice if you want sulfur supplementation alongside phosphorus, since SSP contains 12% sulfur. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How does PAU recommend I split nitrogen on wheat?
output: Apply nitrogen in splits: a starter dose at sowing (depends on phosphorus source — 0 if using DAP, 20 kg urea/acre if using SSP) and the remainder in equal splits at first and second irrigation. Total recommended N is 50 kg/acre on medium fertile soils. The split-application approach reduces nitrogen losses through leaching and better matches uptake to crop demand during tillering and stem elongation. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How much urea should I broadcast at first and second irrigation for timely-sown wheat?
output: For timely sown wheat, broadcast 45 kg urea per acre with each of the first and second irrigations. For wheat sown after mid-December (late sowing), broadcast 35 kg urea per acre at each irrigation. Apply just before the irrigation so the water carries the urea into the root zone. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I sowed wheat after mid-December. How much urea per irrigation?
output: For wheat sown after mid-December, broadcast 35 kg urea per acre at each of the first and second irrigations — less than the 45 kg/acre used for timely sown wheat. The reduced rate matches the shorter growing season and lower yield potential of late-sown wheat. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Rains delayed my second irrigation. When should I apply the urea?
output: If second irrigation is delayed due to rains, broadcast the urea at 55 days after sowing rather than waiting. The crop's nitrogen demand peaks during stem elongation around this time, and missing this window costs yield. The first irrigation's urea should already have been applied. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: Water is stagnating in my wheat field near the second irrigation time. Should I still broadcast urea?
output: No — do not broadcast urea in soil if water is stagnating near the second irrigation. Stagnant water causes denitrification losses. Instead, give two criss-cross sprays of 7.5% urea solution: 15 kg urea dissolved in 200 litres of water per acre, sprayed at 42 days after sowing and again at 54 days after sowing. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: How do I prepare a 7.5% urea solution for foliar spray on wheat?
output: Dissolve 15 kg urea in 200 litres of water per acre — that's a 7.5% solution. Spray as criss-cross sprays at 42 days after sowing and again at 54 days after sowing. Use this method when soil broadcast is impossible due to water stagnation near the second irrigation. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I sowed wheat with Super Seeder. Can I apply urea before irrigation or after?
output: With Super Seeder sown wheat, urea can be applied either before OR after irrigation — both work because the residue cover slows surface vilization. With other methods, apply urea immediately before irrigation. Use the standard rates: 55 kg DAP at sowing and 45 kg urea per acre before first and second irrigation. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.

instruction: I've used Happy Seeder for 4 years. Can I save fertilizer now?
output: Yes — after 3 years of continuous Happy Seeder wheat sowing, from the 4th year onwards reduce urea by 20 kg per acre from the recommended dose. Continuous paddy residue retention builds soil organic carbon and improves nitrogen mineralization, so less external nitrogen is needed. Source: PAU Package of Practices Rabi 2025-26.
